cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Ephesus, and he's just told the Gentiles among them they're not strangers anymore but members of God's household (Ephesians 2:19). Now he starts a new thought, and he opens it by describing himself.

cards.question: Paul starts his new thought by describing himself. What does he call himself?

cards.text: Paul says he's a prisoner for the sake of the Gentiles, and then his sentence just stops mid-thought. Friend, I respect it, because every time my oven timer dings, I leave a sentence hanging and RUN.
So Paul heads down a side road. He says they've surely heard about the stewardship of God's grace that was given to him.

cards.question: Paul says the stewardship of God's grace was given to him for someone. Who?

cards.text: And what's this stewardship about? Paul calls it a mystery, and he tells them how it was made known to him.

cards.question: Paul says the mystery was made known to him by ___.
Paul says he has already written briefly about this mystery.

cards.text: Paul says that when they read what he wrote, they'll understand his insight into the mystery of Christ. And here's the WILD part: people in other generations never had it made known to them the way it's being revealed now.

cards.question: Paul says the Spirit has now revealed the mystery of Christ. To whom?

cards.text: So what's this mystery that stayed under wraps for generation after generation? Paul finally spells it out, and it's about the Gentiles.

cards.question: Through the gospel, what does Paul say is true of the Gentiles?

answers.text: They are fellow heirs in Christ Jesus
They are guests at Israel's table
They are servants to God's people

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles get a smaller share of the promise in Christ Jesus than everyone else.

cards.text: THREE fellows in one verse, friend: fellow heirs, fellow members of the body, fellow partakers of the promise, and nobody gets stuck on the side tray. Not even the lopsided cookie, and believe me, I have BEEN the lopsided cookie!
Now Paul talks about his own part in all this. He became a servant of this gospel.

cards.question: Paul says he became a servant of the gospel by the gift of God's ___.
Paul calls himself the greatest of all the saints.

cards.text: Paul calls himself less than the LEAST of all the saints. Friend, I lived at the very bottom of a junk drawer for years, and even I never found a spot that low.

cards.question: Paul says grace was given to him for a job. What is he to preach to the Gentiles?

cards.text: And it's not only for the Gentiles. Paul's also supposed to shine a light for everyone on the stewardship of this mystery.

cards.question: Paul says this mystery was kept hidden for ages past. Where was it kept?

answers.text: In God who created all things
In the scrolls of the prophets

cards.text: Now Paul zooms WAY out. God had a purpose in all this, and the audience is bigger than you'd ever guess.

cards.question: Through the church, who does Paul say should now be shown the manifold wisdom of God?

answers.text: The rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms
The kings and judges of all the earth
The elders and priests of the house of Israel

cards.text: Through the CHURCH, friend! Regular folks putting God's wisdom on display, and Paul says it lines up with a purpose God accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.

cards.question: Paul calls this purpose a brand new plan God came up with recently.

cards.text: So what does that mean for the people reading this letter? Paul says that in Christ, and through faith in Him, we may enter God's presence.

cards.question: Paul says that in Christ we may only come into God's presence with fear and hesitation.

cards.text: Boldness and CONFIDENCE! Not peeking out all nervous, the way I used to every single time that drawer slid open.
Then Paul brings up the sufferings he's going through for them, and he has a request.

cards.question: Paul brings up his sufferings for the believers. He asks them not to be ___ because of them.
Paul says his sufferings for them are their glory.

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time without a simple statement of who he is. The opening could identify him as Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (Ephesians 1:1), rather than only naming him as the letter's writer.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks for "revelation," a word that has not appeared in the earlier cards. The setup only says that Paul explains how the mystery was made known, so the baker is completing unseen wording rather than using a meaning already established by the walkthrough.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card retells that the mystery stayed hidden through earlier generations, which comes from Ephesians 3:5, but its citation covers only Ephesians 3:6. The citation should include every verse the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The coverage of Ephesians 3:7 never includes that the gift of God's grace was given to Paul through the working of God's power. Cards 1 and 2 cover Paul's servanthood and God's grace, but this part of the verse disappears.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Ephesians 3:11 calls this God's eternal purpose, but neither this card nor the preceding story card says that it is eternal. Marking "a brand new plan God came up with recently" false only establishes that it is not recent and leaves the verse's key description unstated.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question relies on "this purpose" without identifying the purpose in the question itself. Since the preceding story card is no longer visible, it should identify the purpose God accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Paul has a request concerning his sufferings. It gives no basis for choosing the previously unseen word "discouraged" over the also-plausible "ashamed" or "surprised," so the blank becomes a wording guess.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question names only Paul and then uses "them" and "their" without identifying the believers. It should say that Paul's sufferings for the believers are their glory so the question remains self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
